title: Leader: the program and the guests
description: Leader track. An honest practice card, the grid of days, the form and the menu, arrival logistics, the retreat itself and the review after, a plan for a bad day.

units.title: The guest form and the menu
When something goes wrong on the retreat

objectives.text: Describe a practice as a card: format, duration for the group, load, contraindications, touch, with no promises
Build a grid of days that alternates load and rest and treats arrival and departure days as partial
Put together the guest form and a menu by meals, and carry the cost of food into the calculator
Draw up an arrivals list from a single date and set a reserve for guests' mistakes
Run the retreat with a bad-day plan, compare plan with actual and write down terms for next time

checks.question: A pair practice takes 10 minutes per pair, and the group has 16 people. What should the card give as the duration?
options: 10 minutes — that is how long the practice lasts
The duration for the whole group of 16: eight pairs at once plus the explanation, about 25 minutes
160 minutes — 10 for each person
Duration does not matter if the practice is short
checks.explain: The venue and the program need the duration for the group, not for one pair (u1, "Fields of an honest card").

checks.question: Why does the course suggest not putting the main practices on the arrival day?
options: The venue does not allow practices on arrival day
The day is partial: guests arrive tired around lunch, and the main practice would be lost
You cannot eat on arrival day
Insurance requires it
checks.explain: Arrival and departure days are partial. Main practices go on full days (u2, "Partial days").

checks.question: Arrival at lunch, departure after breakfast, six nights. How many dinners are on the menu?
options: Five
Six
Seven
It depends on the chef
checks.explain: A week is counted in meals: with arrival at lunch and departure after breakfast, six nights mean six breakfasts, lunches and dinners (u3, "The edges of the days").

checks.question: Where should the arrival and departure dates live?
options: In each letter to a guest — each with its own copy
In one place — the venue contract, with everything else referring to it
In the flights table, because it is more precise
In each guest's form
checks.explain: The more copies of the dates, the more mismatches. The dates live in the venue contract (u4, "One date — one place").

checks.question: What does comparing plan with actual in the calculator give you after the retreat?
options: Nothing: the retreat is over
It shows the line where the plan was wrong — the basis for the next price and contract
It is only needed for taxes
It helps get money back from the venue
checks.explain: The difference between plan and actual names the line that was wrong. The terms of the next contract come from it (u5, "Plan versus actual").

checks.question: A guest feels unwell on a walk. Which of these is the leader's job?
options: Diagnose and give medicine
Call for help, tell the close contact from the form and write down what happened
Say nothing to the group
Carry on with the programme as if nothing happened
checks.explain: The leader does not treat. They call for help, tell the close contact and record what happened (u6, "A guest who feels unwell").
